rows.line: 🛡️ **F-SRV-4 (attended 2026-10-31; the owner: "Can you check that the server is up to date? There were a lot of security issues (CVEs) recently") — THE GOLD RUSH SERVICES ARE CURRENT; THE ONE EXPOSURE ON THE BOX IS A LEFTOVER: THE OLD AGENT TOWN LANDING, PUBLIC ON PORT 4173, AS ROOT, ON NODE 18.** Measured read-only over ssh at 15:35Z: apt zero pending (security and updates); unattended-upgrades took nginx 1.24.0-2ubuntu7.19 on 2026-10-24 by itself (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479, CVE-2026-97205 and the session-ticket forgery CVE-2026-97629; 7.18 had closed CVE-2026-42533 and CVE-2026-95101); kernel 6.8.0-147 running and newest, no reboot flag; OpenSSL 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 carries the high DTLS fix CVE-2026-84782; OpenSSH 9.6p1-3ubuntu13.20 (the deferred CVE-2026-110928 needs `restrict` keys, and none of the five root keys carries one); Node 26.12.1 on ledger and assayer (26.13.0 of 2026-10-28 is not a security release, the newest nodejs.org advisory is still October's, already covered by F-SRV-2); `/opt/goldrush` npm audit 0 of 47 packages; assayer refusals 0 and backoffs 1 in seven days. The four untriaged nginx CVEs (CVE-2026-116013, -101025, -101019, -108981) name the lua-dns, njs and cache-purge modules: none installed. THE EXPOSURE: `pm2-root.service` (enabled, active) resurrects `/root/code/landing-main/server/index.js`, the beta-onboarding landing from the box's first day, as root on the system `nodejs` 18.19.1 (universe; 9 of the newest 15 nodejs CVEs are needs-triage there), Express 4 with five npm advisories (critical proxy-addr IP spoofing, high body-parser and path-to-regexp DoS, two moderate qs), bound to `*:4173`, HTTP 200 from the internet over plain HTTP (ufw inactive; no cloud firewall fronts the droplet), with POST routes that write `data/store.json`. Nothing uses it: the store is unchanged since 2026-02-02, its log holds seven lines, zero connections; agenttown.app's root serves Gold Rush from nginx (`root /opt/goldrush/site`). Also measured: 2,124 failed ssh logins in 24 h against key-only authentication (noise, not a breach), and the 2026-10-30 16:32Z reboot was a clean systemd reboot following a root login from this network. GATE: owner word "landing go" (`GR_OWNER_APPLY=1 bash scripts/attended/droplet-maintenance.sh landing-stop`; rollback is pm2 resurrect from the stamped dump copy) and "firewall go" (`… firewall`: ufw deny incoming except 22/80/443). Both gated phases landed in this commit; recommended both.

🛡️ **F-SRV-5 (attended 2026-10-31) — THE DROPLET IS NOT ATTACHED TO UBUNTU PRO: NO LIVEPATCH, NO EXPANDED SECURITY MAINTENANCE FOR ITS 410 UNIVERSE PACKAGES.** `pro status` on an unattached machine prints SERVICE/AVAILABLE, so its "livepatch yes" reads as enabled and is not (`is_attached: false`, the canonical-livepatch snap is absent). Main and restricted packages (nginx, openssl, openssh, the kernel) keep receiving fixes until 2029 regardless, and kernel fixes still need the reboot the `status` phase reports. Ubuntu Pro is free for five personal machines and needs the owner's Ubuntu One login once (`pro attach <token>` with the token from ubuntu.com/pro/dashboard), then `pro enable livepatch esm-apps`. Recommended, not urgent; if F-SRV-4 stops the Node 18 landing, esm-apps covers nothing the county runs. GATE: the owner's token; no factory work.

🧹 **F-STO-1 (attended 2026-10-25; the owner: "Can you help clean up the storage needed by Gold Rush … I think Gold Rush uses 600 GB") — THE DISK HELD 1,312 GB OF GOLD RUSH, 86 GB FREE OF 3.6 TB; EVERY SCRATCH WORKTREE CARRIES THE 9–11 GB TRACKED `artifacts/` TREE, SO CHECKOUTS WERE THE MULTIPLIER. Group A (regenerable scratch, no history) removed on the owner's "clean A": 30 merged sibling worktrees `~/Claude/Projects/wt-*` (~300 GB), 21 fire/attended arena checkouts under `~/.goldrush/` (their logs kept), the `land/wt-preview-pub` rsync staging copy (86 GB), four re-land clones in `~/.goldrush/repair` whose tips equal the `candidate/*` branches on GitHub (53 GB; commit maps kept), two old gate worktrees in the primary, eight orphan lane copies inside the history clone whose `.git` files pointed at the primary's live lanes (their 94 untracked unique files, 354 MB of July marketing reels and raw media, archived first to `~/.goldrush/archive/history-local-worktrees-untracked-2026-10-25/`), the stray `Gold%20Rush` folder. Every removal through `git worktree remove` after a merged-branch check and an evidence-only dirt check; 14 items the checks held back were examined by hand (stale checkouts: files equal to blobs of 2026-09-20 / 2026-07-05 commits; a gate worktree whose edits equal main's; control arenas differing only in the pilots symlink) and removed in a second pass. Result: free 86 GB → 782 GB. KEPT AS HISTORY: the history clone's `.git` (106 GB, the only full copy of the private history archive: 443 of its 613 refs are not on GitHub), the film's 23 takes (24 GB), `GoldRush-assets` (13 GB), the primary's `artifacts/`, `logs/`, `tasks/runs` (17 GB), `gr-worktree-evidence`, the run logs. OPEN FOR THE OWNER: `gr-gauntlet` (290 GB: four rider arenas with 19 GB duplicate `.git` copies, ~9 GB dependencies, ~100 GB tracked checkouts, ~40 GB heat evidence to keep), `goldrush-gauntlet` carries 22 unpushed commits (agent memories of heats 11–12), an external drive for the ~200 GB of history, and the structural cure (sparse checkouts without `artifacts/` for scratch worktrees). Log: `~/.goldrush/maintenance/cleanup-2026-10-25.log`.

🔎 **F-CUT-1 (attended 2026-10-09, measured during the Option B cutover) — A STATUS-ONLY EDGE PROBE READS A DEAD API AS HEALTHY.** When the daily Workers/Pages Functions cap is exhausted, Pages serves the SPA's `index.html` with HTTP 200 for `/api/stats`; `scripts/health-watch.sh` and `ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh` reported `api=200` for hours while the county's API was dark, and only the route verifier's JSON demand caught it. Corrective `api-probe-json-1` authored and queued (lane-c). **s3000 verification 08:33Z:** stats returns 200 HTML at the canonical and direct Pages URLs; sampled week-41/week-42 standings reads return valid 200 JSON, so the observed failure is specific to stats and is not evidence that every county endpoint is down. The corrective finished during closing; attended fixture cure `782f9c548` and `apj1` landing process 95225 own its remaining gates. `artifacts/s3000/live-probe.json`, `api-custody.json`.

🧪 **F-ATT-13 (attended 2026-10-31) — `scripts/runner-restart-recipe.test.sh` REDS INTERMITTENTLY ON ITS F-2137-1 STALE-RUNNER ARM, INDEPENDENT OF THE TREE.** Seen while re-running `test:ledger-guards` after the F-SRV-4 commits: the first full battery at 15:49Z passed it; the batteries at 15:53Z and three runs of the guard alone through 16:05Z red both stale-runner assertions ("stayed silent on a stale runner" and "stale runner NOT reported … no inert commits"). A control run of the same guard from an export of the pre-commit scripts (`ca91b8bfe`) reds identically, and the two commits touched only STATUS, docs, the ledger and `scripts/attended/droplet-maintenance.sh`, none of which the guard reads: NOT caused by today's change. The red arm already sleeps a second between its fixture process and its commits, so the second-boundary explanation is out; the fixture's `ps -o lstart` parse (`date -j -f` in `runner_inert_commits`) or the mktemp path are the next suspects. INVESTIGATE-then-fix as a small main-slot corrective when a fire or attended session has the slot; fires should read this red as known until then. **s3477 verification, 2026-10-31:** the unchanged guard passed both stale/current arms with zero failures and two existing PTY custody skips. A retained fixture returned the same commit timestamp for relative, logical /var and physical /private/var pathspecs (all exit 0). Neither suspected path nor the reported red was reproduced; root cause remains UNVERIFIED and this finding stays OPEN. Next: capture the failing arm with its process/commit timestamps before choosing a cure. Evidence: artifacts/s3477/runner-guard-before.txt and path-control.json.
